scope: Bounded follow-up on current Annex L matrix rules in actual producer/consumer paths, beyond the previously reviewed Document wrapper cells. This file does not certify every matrix entry or every possible input tree.

decisions.topic: Whether another PDF 2.0 matrix cell has an active synthetic producer path
decisions.evidence: A search of pdf-transform/src found the merge wrapper as the only path creating a structure element with /NS in the PDF 2.0 standard namespace. Its C3/D3 relations are already covered by the narrow wrapper tests. The archive tagged producer creates Part/P without /NS, so §14.8.6.1 places them in PDF 1.7's default namespace. Merge/split otherwise preserve/prune source relationships while rebuilding hierarchy references; no generic matrix check exists.
decisions.decision: Synthetic-edge search remains bounded to wrapper. Withdraw no-new-test conclusion: B56 proves that pruning valid source children can violate delegated sequence/cardinality.
decisions.test_action: Parent integrated warichu_split_spec_audit; empty boundaries fail and text-bearing boundaries pass.

decisions.evidence: Tree::walk, logical-range extraction and accessibility projection follow /K and map standard roles, but no implementation checks Table L.2 membership. The primary text locates the normative nesting rule in the standard-namespace producer condition and imposes no reader rejection in the reviewed passages.
decisions.decision: Do not add a negative malformed-tree reader test or report acceptance as a conformance failure. Existing readers expose the supplied hierarchy/content; source evidence does not require rejection.
decisions.test_action: None. Existing accessibility/logical-order tests test consumer projections, not matrix conformance.

decisions.topic: Annex L relation to archive Part/P synthesis
decisions.evidence: archive/tagged.rs uses Table 365 Part and Table 366 P, and the emitted structure elements omit /NS. The archive integration test verifies the hierarchy and its content references. The Annex L applicability condition is specifically the PDF 2.0 standard namespace; absent /NS defaults to PDF 1.7 under §14.8.6.1.
decisions.decision: Retain the archive writer as evidence for §14.7 hierarchy construction, but not as Annex L matrix evidence. Its valid duty is governed by PDF 1.7 structure types and archive scope.
decisions.test_action: No new test; existing test already checks the actual Part→P shape and content reachability.

decisions.evidence: ADR 0716's phrase that #83 admits P/Table 'both directions' conflicts with the effective directed table and erratum: P can parent Table at 0..n, while Table cannot parent P from that cell. Its statement that no code reads any Table L.2 cell is stale after ADR 1474/current wrapper logic. ADR 1474 remains accurate for the one wrapper case, role-mapped PDF 2.0 Documents, and the exact root/Document cardinalities.
decisions.decision: Retain ADR 1474 as narrow precedent. Do not rely on ADR 0716 for the directionality of #83 or for current code inventory; prior current-matrix evidence remains authoritative. No new ADR edit proposed in this scratch review.
decisions.test_action: No duplicate of existing corrected #83/#440 cell evidence.

decisions.topic: Current ledger clause L aggregate phrasing
decisions.evidence: The current clause L note says every tree the writer emits keeps the matrix, then identifies the newly synthesized wrapper and says merge/split carry source elements unchanged. This audit located no other PDF 2.0 namespace element synthesis but also found no all-cell check over preserved PDF 2.0 source edges.
decisions.decision: Ledger preservation claim cannot stand as broad verified evidence: B56 contradicts it for a documented valid source form. Do not infer malformed input normalization duty.
decisions.test_action: Record B56; broader cardinalities remain residual.
